gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a Hall effect board with 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth sells under $50 at the makers' own stores today for less than the wired EPOMAKER HE68 Lite ($42.49): Gamakay NS68 tri-mode $39.99 and Aula MINI60 HE $39.09, with Aula stating the MINI60 HE Standard reaches 8K only by cable.
standout_why: Compared against five pages I opened: hlplanet.com (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net's HE68 Lite review (cited), chronicreload.com, deal.ai's under-$50 list, and pcgamer.com (cited), whose article body did not load. HLPlanet lists the NS68 at $42.99 as 'wired or wireless' but gives no wireless polling statement for any sub-$60 board and omits the Ace 60 Pro, HE68 Lite, WIN68 HE and K617 HE. Chronic Reload gives no prices and no connection modes. Deal.ai's ten picks are wired or unlabelled and leave out the NS68 and MINI60 HE. The HE68 Lite review confirms that board is wired only. None puts today's maker-store prices side by side. I did not open setupinsider, thepcjournal, mechanicalkeyboard.net's budget roundup, checkgamingzone or droid4x, so the score is 2 rather than 3.
decides: It moves the pick to the Gamakay NS68, a partner-store board we can link once it has a record. At $36.79 wired it is the lowest-priced 65% board among the four maker stores read (MCHOSE Ace 68 $41.65, EPOMAKER HE68 Lite $42.49, Aula WIN68 HE $42.49), with 8K polling and 0.01 mm rapid-trigger accuracy as Gamakay states them. Its $39.99 tri-mode variant adds wireless for less than ChatGPT's wired all-round pick. The MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro keeps the 60% FPS segment at $37.40 on MCHOSE's store, not the $41.65 ChatGPT showed. Our existing rows (Gamakay NS75 at $63.99, TK75HE V2 at $79.19) are over the $50 line, so the page needs a new NS68 record to qualify. Gamakay's wireless polling rate for the NS68 has to be read before the tri-mode variant is recommended for competitive play.
